context.zh: 史臣曰：自長江徙禦，化龍創業，巨寇乘機而未寧，戎馬交馳而不息，晦重氛於六漠，鼓洪流於八際，天未厭亂，凶旅實繁。
context.idiomatic: The court historian says: Ever since the imperial court moved to the Yangtze and the prince of the dragon prophecy founded his dynasty there, great raiders have seized their opportunity and refused to be still. Warhorses have galloped to and fro without rest. Dense darkness shrouded the six reaches of the world, and great floods surged to its eight limits. Heaven had not yet tired of disorder, and violent armies were many indeed.
context.literal: The court historian says: Ever since the imperial court moved to the Yangtze and the prince of the dragon prophecy founded his dynasty there, great raiders have seized their opportunity and refused to be still. Warhorses have galloped to and fro without rest. Dense darkness shrouded the six reaches of the world, and great floods surged to its eight limits. Heaven had not yet tired of disorder, and violent armies were many indeed.

context.zh: 弋仲越自金方，言歸石氏，抗直詞於暴主，闡忠訓于危朝，貽厥之謀，在乎歸順，鳴哀之義，有足稱焉。
context.idiomatic: Yao Yizhong came from the west and gave his allegiance to the Shi house. He spoke frankly to its violent ruler Shi Hu and gave loyal counsel at a court in peril. The plan he left his descendants was to submit to Jin. The righteousness of his dying words deserves praise.
context.literal: Yao Yizhong came from the west and gave his allegiance to the Shi house. He spoke frankly to its violent ruler Shi Hu and gave loyal counsel at a court in peril. The plan he left his descendants was to submit to Jin. The righteousness of his dying words deserves praise.

context.zh: 取汾、絳，陷許、洛，款僭燕而籓偽蜀，夷隴右而靜河西，俗阜年豐，遠安邇輯，雖楚莊、秦穆何以加焉！
context.idiomatic: He took Fen and Jiang and captured Xu and Luo. He won the allegiance of the rival Yan regime and made the regime in Shu his vassal. He subdued Longyou and pacified Hexi. The people prospered, the harvests were plentiful, distant regions were secure and those close at hand were united. How could King Zhuang of Chu or Duke Mu of Qin have surpassed him?
context.literal: He took Fen and Jiang and captured Xu and Luo, won the submission of the usurping Yan regime and made the pretended regime in Shu his vassal. He subdued Longyou and pacified Hexi. The people prospered, harvests were plentiful, distant regions were secure and those nearby were united. How could King Zhuang of Chu or Duke Mu of Qin have surpassed him?

context.zh: 翻崇詭說，加殊禮于桑門！
context.idiomatic: Instead he exalted teachings the historian deemed deceptive and paid exceptional honors to Buddhist monks.
context.literal: yet he reversed course to honor crafty doctrine and piled special rites on shaven monks!

context.zh: 翻崇詭說，加殊禮于桑門！
context.idiomatic: Instead he exalted teachings the historian deemed deceptive and paid exceptional honors to Buddhist monks.
context.literal: yet he reversed course to honor crafty doctrine and piled special rites on shaven monks!

context.zh: 況乎偽境日侵，寧堪永貴之役！
context.idiomatic: How, then, could a realm whose borders were daily encroached upon bear the cost of building the Buddhist stupa at Yonggui?
context.literal: How much less could a usurping regime, its borders daily encroached upon, bear the labor of construction at Yonggui?

context.zh: 儲用殫竭，山林有稅，政荒威挫，職是之由，坐致淪胥，非天喪也。
context.idiomatic: Reserves were exhausted, and even the hills and forests were taxed. Government fell into neglect and authority was broken. These were the causes. They brought ruin upon themselves; Heaven did not destroy them.
context.literal: Stores were exhausted, hills and forests taxed; government wild, awe broken—this is the reason; sitting to bring ruin—Heaven did not destroy them.

context.zh: 王師杖順，弭節而下長安；
context.idiomatic: With right on its side, the Jin army advanced at an easy pace and took Chang’an.
context.literal: With right on its side, the Jin army advanced at an easy pace and took Chang’an.

context.zh: 凶嗣失圖，系組而降軹道。
context.idiomatic: The wicked heir, at a loss for any plan, surrendered with the cord about his neck, like the Qin ruler at Zhidao.
context.literal: the wicked heir lost his plan, tied cord and surrendered at Zhidao.

relevantFindings.reason: The Qin ruler in Shiji 6 surrendered with the neck cord at Zhidao; the appraisal assimilates Hong's surrender to that precedent. Record the action as historiographical imagery rather than a separate literal relocation. https://zh.wikisource.org/wiki/史記/卷006
